content.title: Complex sentences: upgrade band-5 writing to band 7–8
content.instructions: Each prompt is written at about band 5: short, simple sentences joined by 'and', 'but' or 'so'. Rewrite it as ONE well-controlled complex sentence (or two at most) using relative, adverbial or noun clauses. Keep the original meaning; you may improve vocabulary as well.

items.prompt: The graph shows car sales. Car sales went up until 2008. Then they went down a lot.
accepted_answers: The graph shows that car sales rose steadily until 2008, when they fell sharply.
items.model_answer: The graph shows that car sales rose steadily until 2008, after which they fell sharply.
items.explanation: A noun clause (shows that …) turns the chart description into one sentence, and a relative clause with 'when' or 'after which' links the turning point to what followed, avoiding the repetitive subject 'car sales … they'.

items.prompt: Some people think university should be free. This is because education helps everyone.
accepted_answers: Some people argue that university should be free because education benefits society as a whole.
items.model_answer: Some people argue that university education should be free of charge because a well-educated population benefits society as a whole.
items.explanation: A noun clause (argue that …) reports the opinion, and an adverbial clause of reason (because …) replaces the separate 'This is because' sentence, which examiners often see as a band-5 pattern.

items.prompt: I like living in a big city. There are many things to do. But it is very expensive.
accepted_answers: Although living in a big city is very expensive, I enjoy it because there is always something to do.
items.model_answer: Although city life can be extremely expensive, I really enjoy it because there's always something going on, whether it's a concert, an exhibition or just a new restaurant to try.
items.explanation: An 'although' clause of concession replaces 'But', and a 'because' clause gives the reason, so the Speaking Part 3 answer becomes one fluent, complex sentence. Never use 'although' and 'but' together.

items.prompt: Many old people live alone. They often feel lonely. The government should help them.
accepted_answers: Elderly people who live alone often feel lonely, so the government should do more to support them.
items.model_answer: Elderly people who live alone often suffer from loneliness, which is why the government should provide more community support for them.
items.explanation: A defining relative clause (who live alone) identifies the group without a separate sentence, and 'which is why' is a sentence-relative clause that links the problem to the solution.

items.prompt: Tourism brings a lot of money. It also damages the environment. This is a big problem.
accepted_answers: While tourism brings considerable economic benefits, it also damages the environment, which is a serious problem.
items.model_answer: While tourism brings considerable economic benefits, it also causes significant environmental damage, which presents a serious dilemma for many coastal communities.
items.explanation: A contrast clause (While …) balances the two sides in one sentence, and a non-defining relative clause with 'which' comments on the whole idea instead of starting a new sentence with 'This'.

items.prompt: The factory is in the south of the town. It produces paper. It employs 500 people.
accepted_answers: The factory, which is in the south of the town and produces paper, employs 500 people.
items.model_answer: The paper factory, which is located in the south of the town, employs 500 people.
items.explanation: Three short sentences about the same noun can be merged with a non-defining relative clause (which is located …) placed between commas, keeping the most important fact (employs 500 people) in the main clause.

items.prompt: Children play computer games a lot. So they do not do exercise. So they become overweight.
accepted_answers: Because children who play computer games a lot do little exercise, they often become overweight.
items.model_answer: Children who spend long hours playing computer games tend to take little physical exercise, which makes them more likely to become overweight.
items.explanation: Repeating 'So … So …' creates a chain of simple sentences. A defining relative clause (who spend long hours …) and a 'which' clause expressing the result show the cause-and-effect relationship far more precisely.

items.prompt: People eat a lot of fast food. The reason is they are busy.
accepted_answers: The main reason why people eat so much fast food is that they are very busy.
items.model_answer: The main reason why so many people rely on fast food is that they lead increasingly busy lives.
items.explanation: The pattern 'The reason why … is that …' uses two clauses: a relative clause after 'reason' and a noun clause after 'is'. Avoid 'The reason is because …', which is redundant.

items.prompt: Some people say technology makes us lonely. I don't agree. We can talk to our friends online.
accepted_answers: Although some people claim that technology makes us lonely, I disagree because it allows us to talk to our friends online.
items.model_answer: Although some people claim that technology has made us more isolated, I would argue that it actually allows us to stay in touch with friends whom we would otherwise rarely see.
items.explanation: This version combines three clause types: a concession clause (Although …), two noun clauses (claim that …, argue that …) and a defining relative clause (friends whom we would otherwise rarely see). This is the range examiners look for at band 7 and above.
